figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2 | Heterologous expression of the taa BGC and structural characteri­
zation of a thiazole acylsulfenic acid. a, The taa BGC in Streptomyces sp. 
CNT360 encodes a hybrid PKS–NRPS (TaaE, TaaF and TaaG) and three putative 
tailoring enzymes (TaaH: group B FPMO; TaaI: CoA-transferase; TaaJ: acyl-CoA 
synthetase) responsible for the biosynthesis of a thiazole acylsulfenic acid.  
b, LC–PDA analysis of ethyl acetate extract of the supernatant from the hetero­
logous expression strain M1152_taa indicates the production of two compounds, 
carboxy-presulfenicin (1) and sulfenicin (2) that are not produced by the WT 
M1152. c, UV absorbance profiles and IR spectra of carboxy-presulfenicin (1)

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3 | In vivo deletion of genes in M1152_taa to probe biosynthetic function. 
a, The hypothesized biosynthetic pathway of sulfenicin (2). TaaF, a putative 
iterative type I PKS, is expected to initiate assembly with propionyl-CoA and 
then elongate three times with methylmalonyl coenzyme A (mMCoA), reducing 
and dehydrating each module as necessary to form the aliphatic chain seen in 
carboxy-presulfenicin (1). TaaG, a putative NRPS, is then proposed to incorporate 
and subsequently cyclize l-cysteine to form the thiazole moiety in carboxy-
presulfenicin (1). Once the backbone is assembled, TaaJ, TaaI and TaaH are 
predicted to incorporate a sulfur and hydroxylate it to form sulfenicin (2). b, PDA

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4 | In vitro reconstitution of acylsulfenic acid-synthesizing enzymes.  
a, The hypothesized biosynthetic pathway for the acylsulfenic acid functional 
group in sulfenicin (2). TaaJ first generates 1-CoA from carboxy-presulfenicin (1), 
after which TaaI incorporates sulfur from primary metabolic pathways to yield 
thio-presulfenicin (5), which is finally hydroxylated by TaaH to yield the final 
product, sulfenicin (2). AMP, adenosine monophosphate; PPi, pyrophosphate;
